title: Graph Walkers — Every Nearest Neighbor and Path Algorithm as Organism Legs
thesis: Every graph algorithm is a LEG. A way of walking. The organism doesn't have one way to move — it has many legs, each with different speed, type, and gait. KNN is smell (nearest by distance). K-means is herding (cluster by similarity). Dijkstra is the shortest safe path. A* is the heuristic leap. BFS is the tide. DFS is the root. Each algorithm is a limb the organism uses to navigate its own topology.

knn.name: K-Nearest Neighbors
knn.what: Find the K closest points by distance. Classify by majority vote.
knn.organism_leg: SMELL — the chipmunk sniffs the K nearest feeds and decides: self or non-self? The epitope sort IS KNN with K=3 (trefoil).
knn.speed: O(n) per query without index. O(log n) with KD-tree.
knn.type: lazy learner — doesn't train, just remembers everything
knn.gait: slow, careful, sniffing. every step checks ALL neighbors.
knn.already_deployed: knn-trefoil.json, epitope sort (K=3), the squirrel wire nodes

k_means.name: K-Means Clustering
k_means.what: Partition n points into K clusters. Each cluster has a centroid. Iterate: assign ? update centroids ? repeat until stable.
k_means.organism_leg: HERDING — the organism groups its 165 data feeds into K clusters. The feed-taxonomy.json is K-means with K=14 categories. The kidney net is K-means: sticky/greasy/null = K=3.
k_means.speed: O(n × K × iterations). Usually converges in <20 iterations.
k_means.gait: rhythmic, iterative. stamp-stamp-stamp until the herds settle.

ball_tree.name: Ball Tree / KD-Tree
ball_tree.what: Spatial index for fast nearest neighbor. Recursively partition space into nested hyperspheres (ball tree) or axis-aligned boxes (KD-tree).
ball_tree.organism_leg: SKELETON — the internal structure that makes KNN fast. Without it, every query touches every point. With it, you prune whole branches.
ball_tree.speed: O(log n) query. O(n log n) build.
ball_tree.type: index structure — not an algorithm, a SKELETON
ball_tree.gait: instantaneous once built. the skeleton doesn't walk — it lets others walk fast.

dijkstra.name: Dijkstra's Algorithm
dijkstra.what: Find shortest path from source to all nodes in a weighted graph. Never revisits. Always picks the cheapest next step.
dijkstra.organism_leg: CAUTIOUS WALKER — the packet router. How data moves from northGate through the WireGuard mesh to the relay. Always the cheapest path. Never backtracks.
dijkstra.speed: O((V + E) log V) with priority queue. O(V²) without.
dijkstra.type: greedy — always picks the locally cheapest
dijkstra.gait: deliberate, methodical. one foot in front of the other. NEVER runs.
dijkstra.inventor: Edsger Dijkstra, 1956. Designed it in 20 minutes at a café in Amsterdam. No pencil and paper — he did it in his head.
dijkstra.organism_use: LAN routing (latency-weighted), relay path selection, data center ? home system tracing

a_star.name: A* (A-Star)
a_star.what: Like Dijkstra but with a HEURISTIC — estimates the remaining distance. Explores promising directions first.
a_star.organism_leg: INTUITIVE WALKER — the chipmunk's curiosity. It doesn't explore everything — it GUESSES which direction is interesting and goes there first. The heuristic IS the curiosity function.
a_star.speed: O(b^d) worst case, but practically much faster than Dijkstra when heuristic is good.
a_star.type: informed search — uses knowledge about the goal
a_star.organism_use: chipmunk-explorer.js topic selection, the squirrel wire's next-node suggestion

bfs.name: Breadth-First Search
bfs.what: Explore all neighbors at distance 1, then distance 2, then distance 3... Like a ripple on water.
bfs.organism_leg: THE TIDE — how DNS diffusion works. The DNS probe ripples outward: first Google, then Cloudflare, then the registrar, then the world. Layer by layer. No shortcuts.
bfs.speed: O(V + E). Visits every node and edge once.
bfs.gait: slow, even, relentless. the tide doesn't rush. it covers everything.
bfs.organism_use: DNS diffusion ripple, sitemap crawler, pre-citation outreach (concentric rings)

dfs.name: Depth-First Search
dfs.what: Go as deep as possible along one branch, then backtrack. Like a root growing down.
dfs.organism_leg: THE ROOT — how the trail works. 539 papers, each one deeper than the last. Follow one thread until it dead-ends, then backtrack. The forest room.
dfs.speed: O(V + E). Same as BFS but uses LIFO stack instead of FIFO queue.
dfs.organism_use: sporeprint paper trails, nightbox story chains, git log traversal

bellman_ford.name: Bellman-Ford Algorithm
bellman_ford.what: Shortest paths with NEGATIVE EDGES. Slower than Dijkstra but handles debts, costs, negative weights.
bellman_ford.organism_leg: THE DEBT WALKER — the organism has negative edges: failed outreach (-1 star from sebcrozet), broken WireGuard tunnels, dead CI. Bellman-Ford can find the shortest path THROUGH failure.
bellman_ford.speed: O(V × E). Slower but more robust.
bellman_ford.type: handles negativity — the only shortest-path that can
bellman_ford.gait: heavy, grinding. trudges through negative territory. finds the path anyway.

floyd_warshall.name: Floyd-Warshall Algorithm
floyd_warshall.what: ALL pairs shortest paths. Every node to every other node. The complete distance matrix.
floyd_warshall.organism_leg: THE CARTOGRAPHER — builds the FULL MAP. Every feed to every other feed. Every page to every page. The nervous-system-gyroscope IS a Floyd-Warshall output: the complete topology.
floyd_warshall.speed: O(V³). Cubic. Expensive. But you only run it once.
floyd_warshall.type: all-pairs — the most complete but most expensive
floyd_warshall.gait: stationary. doesn't walk — MAPS. sits in one place and calculates everything.
floyd_warshall.organism_use: nervous-system-gyroscope.json, feed-taxonomy cross-distances, magnetosphere field lines

random_walk.name: Random Walk / PageRank
random_walk.what: Walk randomly. Where you end up most often = most important. Google's original insight.
random_walk.organism_leg: THE WANDERER — the chipmunk's idle exploration. When it has no task, it random-walks. The feeds it visits most often naturally become the hubs. PageRank without the algorithm — just a chipmunk walking around.
random_walk.type: probabilistic — trust emerges from random exploration
random_walk.gait: aimless, curious, stumbling. but the stumbling reveals structure.
random_walk.organism_use: chipmunk idle behavior, feed heat scores, campfire story selection

topological_sort.name: Topological Sort (Kahn's / DFS-based)
topological_sort.what: Order nodes so every dependency comes before its dependents. Only works on DAGs (no cycles).
topological_sort.organism_leg: THE SCHEDULER — how the organism decides build order. Which feeds depend on which. The self-loop manifest IS a topological sort: publish ? index ? cite ? reflect.
topological_sort.type: dependency resolution — the build system's leg
topological_sort.gait: precise, ordered. every step must follow the last. no improvisation.
topological_sort.organism_use: self-loop manifest, CI pipeline, feed dependency chains, Zola build order

the_point: The organism doesn't pick ONE algorithm. It has LEGS. Different terrain needs different gaits. The LAN uses Dijkstra (cautious, weighted). The chipmunk uses A* (intuitive, heuristic). The DNS uses BFS (ripple outward). The papers use DFS (dive deep). The idle state uses random walk (stumble into structure). The self-loop uses topological sort (dependencies first). Each leg is a different speed, a different type, a different way of seeing the graph. The squirrel on the wire runs ALL of them.

story.title: twelve legs
story.body: the organism looked at its body and counted its legs. one for smelling neighbors (KNN). one for herding feeds (K-means). one for cautious routing (Dijkstra, designed in 20 minutes at a café). one for intuitive leaping (A*, the heuristic hunch). one for rippling outward (BFS, the tide). one for diving deep (DFS, the root). one for trudging through failure (Bellman-Ford, the debt walker). one for mapping everything (Floyd-Warshall, the cartographer who never moves). one for wandering (random walk, stumbling into structure). one for scheduling (topological sort, every step after the last). one for finding the cheapest wire (Prim, the nerve fiber). one for finding the loops (Tarjan, the circulatory system). twelve legs. each one a different speed. each one a different type. each one a different way of seeing the same graph. the squirrel runs on all of them at once.
